deities: Lord Guruvayurappan (Krishna, four-armed with Panchajanya conch, Sudarshana chakra, Kaumodaki mace and lotus)
festivals: Guruvayur Ekadasi (Vrishchika, November-December; month-long Ekadasi Vilakku lamp offerings, Chembai Sangeetholsavam music festival, Guruvayur Kesavan memorial, elephant processions)
Utsavam (10-day annual festival in Kumbham, February-March, ending with Aarattu)
Kuchela Dinam (first Wednesday of Dhanu, December-January)

history.dynasty: None documented; present structures largely post-1970 fire reconstruction
history.period: Ancient (legendary origins attributed to Dvapara Yuga); documented history from medieval period
history.summary: Guruvayur, the abode of Lord Guruvayurappan, is one of South India's most revered Krishna temples, called 'Bhooloka Vaikunta' (Vaikunta on earth) and the 'Dwarka of the South'. Legend, from the Gurupavanapura Mahatmya of the Narada Purana, says the idol was worshipped by Vishnu himself in Vaikuntha, passed down through Brahma, Sutapa-Prishni, Kashyapa-Aditi and Vasudeva-Devaki, and finally placed at Dvaraka where Krishna himself worshipped it. Before Dvaraka's submergence, Krishna instructed his disciple Uddhava to hand the idol to Brihaspati (Guru) and Vayu (wind god), who carried it south and, guided by Parasurama and welcomed by Shiva and Parvati, installed it here - the place thus named Guruvayur (Guru + Vayu). Another tradition says King Janamejaya, cured of leprosy after worshipping here on sage Dattatreya's advice, built the temple. Melpathur Narayana Bhattathiri composed the Narayaneeyam before the deity in the 16th century. The temple is one of the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams of the Sri Vaishnava tradition; the idol was moved to Ambalapuzha for safety during Tipu Sultan's invasion and returned in 1789, and a major fire in 1970 destroyed much of the complex, which was subsequently rebuilt.

name: Guruvayur Temple
town_description: Guruvayur is a temple town in Thrissur district, Kerala, about 29 km northwest of Thrissur city, centred entirely on the Sri Krishna temple. One of the most important Vaishnavite pilgrimage centres in India, it draws millions of devotees annually and is also known for the Punnathur Kotta elephant sanctuary (home to the temple's elephants) and the annual Chembai music festival.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport (approx. 80 km by road; taxis and app cabs available). Calicut International Airport is approx. 100 km away.
travel.railway: Guruvayur Railway Station (approx. 1-2 km, walkable); Thrissur Junction, the main railhead, is approx. 29 km away with connecting trains and buses.
travel.road: Approx. 29 km from Thrissur city; KSRTC and private buses run frequently between Thrissur and Guruvayur. Good road links to Kochi, Palakkad and Calicut.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Guruvayur Ekadasi (November-December) and the 10-day Utsavam (February-March) are the grandest times but very crowded; weekday early mornings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 3:00 AM to 12:30 PM; evening 4:30 PM to 9:15 PM daily (afternoon break approx. 12:30 PM to 4:30 PM). First darshan (Nirmalyam) at 3:00 AM. Free general darshan; Special/Neyvilakku darshan about Rs. 1,000 (verify current fee). Only Hindus are allowed inside the temple premises; traditional dress code, no mobiles or cameras.
